title: The Creation and Aesthetic Appreciation of Architecture
review_question: What are the cognitive and neural bases of architectural creativity and the aesthetic appreciation of architectural design features?

findings.antecedent: Personality variables (flexibility, achievement via independence, low self-control, cognitive flexibility, openness, receptivity, concern with deeper meanings)
findings.quote: the results demonstrated that personality variables play an important role in distinguishing creative architects from their less creative counterparts
cognitive abilities (e.g., IQ) were shown to be unrelated to variations in creativity.

findings.antecedent: Flexible interplay between associative and inferential processes
findings.source: Abstract, The Story from the Brain
findings.quote: architectural creativity has been linked to the flexible interplay between associative and inferential processes

findings.antecedent: Ordinary thought processes working on exceptionally rich content
findings.source: Abstract, Cognitive Bases of Architectural Creativity
findings.quote: high-level creativity in architecture could in part be driven by ordinary thought processes working on exceptionally rich content.
people exhibit a preference for curvilinear over rectilinear design
people prefer rooms with higher than lower ceilings
perceived enclosure affected both aesthetic judgments as well as approach-avoidance decisions: subjects were more likely to find open rooms beautiful

findings.antecedent: Cognitive abilities (fluid intelligence, executive function, working memory)
findings.quote: recent studies have shown that creativity as measured by divergent thinking tasks is in fact strongly related to cognitive abilities
fluid intelligence exerted a positive effect on originality, which in turn exerted a positive effect on trait creativity.

findings.antecedent: Divergent thinking ability (Alternate Uses Task scores)
findings.quote: divergent thinking ability ... did not predict the likelihood that an architect's work would appear on either list of AIA's most popular buildings.
architectural creativity ratings predicted the likelihood that an architect's work would appear on both lists of most popular buildings.
the design vs. problem-solving condition revealed greater activation in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex

findings.consequent: Impaired preliminary (ill-structured) phase of design process
findings.quote: PF's suboptimal design was largely due to difficulties in the preliminary phase of the design process.

findings.consequent: Maintenance of indeterminate representations during problem solving
findings.quote: the right prefrontal cortex appears to enable the maintenance of indeterminate representations during problem solving.
aesthetic preference for curvilinear spaces was correlated with activation in the anterior cingulate cortex.
contour had no effect on approach-avoidance decisions.

findings.consequent: Likelihood to opt to enter rooms
findings.quote: Behaviorally, as predicted, subjects were more likely to opt to enter rooms with higher ceilings.

findings.consequent: Activation in precuneus and middle frontal gyrus
findings.quote: in the context of beauty judgments higher ceilings activated the precuneus and the middle frontal gyrus
the effect of ceiling height did not extend to approach-avoidance decisions.

findings.antecedent: Open rooms (less perceived enclosure) during beauty judgments
findings.consequent: Activation in middle and superior temporal gyri
findings.quote: When judging beauty open rooms activated the middle and superior temporal gyri significantly more than enclosed rooms.

findings.consequent: Activation in anterior midcingulate cortex (with direct projections from amygdala)
findings.quote: enclosed spaces activated the anterior midcingulate cortex, the region within the cingulate cortex with the most direct projections from the amygdala.

findings.consequent: Cortisol reactivity to stress, Cortisol recovery rate
findings.quote: participants in the enclosed condition exhibited greater cortisol reactivity to the stress condition and continued to show greater levels of cortisol at recovery.

synthesis_conclusions: Recent research has advanced the understanding of architectural creativity by highlighting the contributions of cognitive processes and content, building on classic work.
There is a better understanding of the neural bases of creative design in architecture.
Insights are emerging into how the brain and physiology respond to variations in specific design features of architecture.
These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of creativity and aesthetics in architecture.
evidence_gaps: The limitations of fMRI in studying approach-avoidance decisions in real-life settings suggest a need for more ecologically valid research methods.
Further research is needed to fully understand the factors distinguishing highly creative from less creative individuals, particularly regarding the content of thought.
The precise mechanisms underlying the link between aesthetic judgments and approach-avoidance decisions require further investigation.
limitations: The fMRI scanner setting may not offer sufficient fidelity for studying approach-avoidance decisions that determine behavioral choices in real-life settings.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The aesthetic appreciation of architectural forms is influenced by their collative properties (e.g., complexity, novelty, surprisingness) which modulate arousal and hedonic value.
Architectural creativity is a function of domain-relevant skills, creativity-relevant processes, and intrinsic task motivation, which can be influenced by environmental factors.

mechanism_chain.description: Personality variables, such as cognitive flexibility and openness, influence an individual's cognitive processes, leading to enhanced divergent thinking and problem-solving approaches, which in turn contribute to architectural creativity by facilitating the generation of novel and appropriate solutions.
